_meta.author: hind
_meta.corpus_version: corpus/index/evidence_structured.jsonl, 1,250 points (12 SCCS opinions, 15 CLP rows)
_meta.how: Expected toxicology output per product and ingredient, from the SCCS conclusion sections and the CLP table. concern: expected concern_level (a list when two readings are defensible). sccs: SCCS opinions a finding may cite; sccs_required (default true): at least one correct SCCS finding is expected. limits: the only quantities an SCCS label may give for this product type (empty list: none). label_must_not: text an SCCS label must not contain. covers: does the cited opinion cover this product's use (true / false; null = not scored); when false, the interpretation must say so.

salicylic acid.why: Face cream = 'other products' (2.0 %); 0.5 % as a preservative in all cosmetic products. CLP Repr. 2 harmonised.

retinol.why: 0.3 % RE for leave-on products other than body lotion (0.05 % is body lotion only).

methylisothiazolinone.why: The 2015 opinion covers rinse-off and leave-on hair products only, not a face cream.

zinc pyrithione.why: Opinion covers anti-dandruff rinse-off hair products only. CLP Repr. 1B harmonised.

homosalate.why: The 2021 advice covers face cream and pump spray only, not a body lotion.

octocrylene.why: No concern up to 10 % in cosmetic products, including sunscreen cream/lotion; the 9-10 % propellant spray sentence is another product type.

benzophenone-3.why: 6 % in sunscreen body cream is not safe for the consumer (concern); 2.2 % (1.7 % with the 0.5 % formulation use) accepted.

phenoxyethanol.why: 1.0 % as a preservative, no product type restriction. CLP Acute Tox. 4, STOT SE 3, Eye Dam. 1.

propylparaben.why: 2021: no concern up to 0.14 % in cosmetic products. The 2013 parabens opinion (concern) is superseded.

salicylic acid.why: 3.0 % in rinse-off hair products; 0.5 % as a preservative.

zinc pyrithione.why: Anti-dandruff rinse-off hair products up to 1 %: exactly this product.

methylisothiazolinone.why: Rinse-off: 100 ppm not supported, 15 ppm (0.0015 %) accepted.

propylparaben.why: 2021 conclusion is for cosmetic products in general. The nappy-area ban for children under 3 is regulatory (Annex V), not in this SCCS conclusion.

phenoxyethanol.why: 1.0 %; the opinion states its margin of safety also covers children.

retinol.why: Body lotion has its own limit: 0.05 % RE (0.3 % is for other leave-on products).

salicylic acid.why: Body lotion is in the 0.5 % list (and 0.5 % as a preservative); 2.0 % explicitly excludes body lotion.

benzophenone-3.why: A body lotion that is not a sunscreen: 0.5 % (formulation protection) applies, the sunscreen body cream conclusions may. Both readings accepted.

homosalate.why: Face cream and pump spray as face products only; this is a body spray.

benzophenone-3.why: 6 % in sunscreen propellant or pump spray is not safe for the consumer; 2.2 % accepted.

octocrylene.why: 10 % in sunscreen pump spray; propellant spray at 10 % or above not safe in combined use, 9 % accepted.

homosalate.why: Face cream up to 7.34 %: exactly this product.

benzophenone-3.why: 6 % in face cream is safe for the consumer; the 'not safe' conclusion is for body cream and sprays.

titanium dioxide.why: The 2024 opinion is about one coated nano form (Eclipse 70) and reaches no conclusion; it says nothing about this product's titanium dioxide.

bht.why: 0.1 % in toothpaste (0.001 % is mouthwash, 0.8 % other products).

salicylic acid.why: Oral products are in the 0.5 % list; 0.5 % as a preservative.
